text.p: Mining and civil engineering group Macmahon Holdings Ltd said on Monday it was confident of a buoyant earnings performance in its 1996/97 financial year in the absence of a deterioration in the Australian economy.

"We have started the new financial year with a record forward order book and with solid prospects for winning additional new contracts throughout Australia and in Asia during the opening half of the new financial year," MacMahon's chief executive, Graeme Beissel said in a statement.
Mcmahon earlier said its net profit for the year to June 30, 1996 jumped to A$15.74 million from A$8.78 million.

Beissel said the outlook for the contracting mining sector generally remained strong with major new mining and mining-related infrastructure projects already under way or planned throughout most Australian states and territories, and in South East Asia.
"New opportunities are also filtering through in the Australian civil engineering sector," he said.
Macmahon shares closed two cents higher at 88 cents.
